provenance.title: VBA God Module
provenance.method: git archive <commit> | tar -x -C <dir> — then the in-gate mirror (test/fixtures/acorn-babel-mirror.mts over the acorn branch, function-count-mirror.mts over the regex branch) scores every tracked member of CODE_EXTS in both trees; the external run-analysis.mjs sandbox uses the regex branch and misses object-literal methods, so the mirror is the in-gate measurement.
provenance.metric: patterns[name === "VBA God Module"].files — analyzed files where isCode !== false && functions.length > 20 (index.html:1414 detectPatterns `vbaGodFiles`). `VBA God Module` is `God Object` (> 15) at a higher ceiling over the same parser count. `functions` comes from the parser: for `.js/.jsx/.ts/.tsx/.mjs/.cjs/.vue/.svelte` the served UI parses with acorn (after Babel strips TS/JSX), so object-literal methods and arrow properties count; for `.py/.go/.rs/...` the regex extractor counts. This fixture's mirror re-runs both branches over the CURRENT tree and over the pinned base commit, so a regression that leaves a split module over the ceiling, or a module that was never really reduced, cannot pass.
provenance.filesNote: `codeFiles` is the count of tracked files whose extension the analyzer scores (the pinned `codeExts`, mirrored as `CODE_EXTS`), measured in-gate from `git ls-tree` at the base commit and `git ls-files` in the delivered tree. `after.codeFiles === before.codeFiles + 58 siblings from this refactor + five siblings from #2034 merged into main` proves the drop did not come from deleting files. `.mts`/`.json`/`.md` are not in `codeExts`, so the mirror and this fixture add no scored file.
provenance.filedNote: the issue was filed with 25 files at analyzedAt 1791804971015 against the then-main. That snapshot predates #2006 (the two Python test modules still counted 21 each) and #2057. The pinned base re-measures 25 as well, but with those two Python modules already split (`alreadyUnder`) and two files the issue did not cite (disk_space_test.go, fp-filter.js) newly over the ceiling (`deferred`).
provenance.afterNote: `after` is the delivered working tree after #2034 advanced main beyond the pinned base. Every one of the 25 filed files is either reduced (23) or was already under the ceiling at the pinned base (2); the 17 modules a prior attempt deferred — the 16 `.rs` files and `server.py` — are now split too, each into siblings of the same module tree, so no cited module is left flagged. #2034 also reduced the uncited `disk_space_test.go`; only `fp-filter.js` remains flagged.

baseAdvance.reason: After the pinned base, #2034 added five scored siblings and reduced the uncited disk-space test below the threshold; #2035 added four scored siblings (`codeflow/bridge_js.py`, `ui/src/rpc/client/replay.rs`, `ui/src/protocol/events.rs`, `ui/tests/session_controls/journey.rs`); #2053 added ten scored files (eight Go build-contract tests plus scripts/net-bytes.sh and scripts/measure-cold-build.sh).

tradeoffs.vbaGodModule: 25 -> 1 flagged file (-24): every cited module now lands at or below the 20-declaration ceiling. The reduced modules carried object-literal stubs, JSON-kind extractors, dialog helpers, a 93-declaration ExtensionAPI mock and whole Rust test suites the parser counts as declarations; cohesive blocks moved verbatim into siblings of the same module tree, and each reduced module keeps its public surface (spread/merge/re-export barrels in TS, `mod`/`pub use` in Rust, sibling imports in Python), so no importer changed. The main branch also includes #2034's split siblings.
tradeoffs.godObject: the expected co-benefit (VBA God Module is a strict subset of God Object): 36 -> 27 in the delivered tree. Ten of the new `.rs` test siblings land at 16-20 — they are cohesive test groups split out of a God Object parent, so the family total is unchanged — and the in-gate oracle measures the delivered tree against the pinned base.
tradeoffs.functions: No test was added, removed or renamed: the suites still run the same tests, `mock-pi.ts` composes the same stub object, the Rust module trees still hold the same declarations (the oracle checks the per-family declaration total is conserved), and every public export keeps its name.
tradeoffs.approach: verbatim moves plus re-export barrels: TS modules spread/merge factories and kind tables and re-export the moved types; the Rust modules move impl/fn blocks into child modules declared with `mod` (integration-test children reached through `#[path]`) and re-export the public items; `server.py` became five sibling modules (`config`, `report_store`, `analysis_run`, `repo_identity`, `ui_rewrites`) whose imports keep the served contract, with the Dockerfile `COPY`/`py_compile` set updated. `npm test`, `npm run tsc:extensions`, `go test ./cmd/cheasee-pi/` and `rustfmt --check` are the verification burden.
tradeoffs.notDone: one file flagged on the delivered tree but NOT cited by #2036 (`fp-filter.js`) stays flagged; it is owned by the long-file / anti-pattern issues that share the same file set.
tradeoffs.rustVerification: the pipeline image has no C linker, so `cargo check` cannot run even though a `rustc` toolchain is present. The split was verified with a module-tree resolver over every `mod` declaration plus `rustfmt --check` over all crate roots (which parses every reachable module); the browser build remains the first full type-check.

alreadyUnder.reason: cited by the issue but already under the pinned base's ceiling: #2006 split these two Python test modules (21 declarations each on the filed snapshot) before this refactor started, so re-measuring the pinned base does not flag them. They stay cited-and-covered rather than dropped from the ledger.

deferred.reason: still flagged on the delivered tree but NOT cited by #2036; owned by the long-file / anti-pattern issues that share the same file set, not by this reduction.
